name: Aaliyah
notes: The lane's most influential rhythm-first singer, on Timbaland and Static Major from 1996 with an R. Kelly-era 1994–95 tail. The research states "93 is the house tempo (straight, backbeat 2&4)", so the mode is 93 and `halfTime` is false. The entry declares "BPM 78–120" and puts the "110–120 cuts" on half-time, so the straight band it leaves is 78–109 exactly, and that is the band encoded; the 110–120 half-time cuts are a different backbeat class and are deliberately not folded into this grid. Three drum deltas are quoted: "syncopated 16th kick pairs" (syncopation 0.78 and a tresillo lean far past the parent's, secondary anchor on `2a`), "snare pushed a 16th late" (an 8–16 ms off-grid push), and "hats swapped for tuned clicks/baby-coo samples" with "hard silence used as an accent" — a non-continuous hat at 0.14 and a five-lane percussion bed at −3 dB, the most forward percussion in this batch, plus a real `beatSkipProb`. Harmony is "single-chord or two-chord modal beds (Dorian/Aeolian), so the melody carries all the interest" — the single-chord family leads, scales are weighted onto Dorian, and `chordDurationBeats` runs to 32. "Breathy, close-mic'd, low note-density, phrases starting off the downbeat" is the 2–6 density, the empty-bar bias and the small motif; "harmony stacks are unison-plus-octave rather than triadic" is why the counter is `octave_echo` alone. The low end is "sub-808 with portamento slides between root and 5th… bass and kick alternate rather than stack" — a real bass part with a 0.5 glide and root-fifth cells, so no `drums.bass808` block, which would have silenced it. ⚠ The era start is the entry's "R. Kelly-era 1994–95". Its end year is INFERRED: the entry reads "Timbaland/Static Major from 1996" and states no closing year, so the 2001 here is this author's reading of where the catalogue stops and is not in the text. ⚠ The other INFERRED parameters are all velocity, density and jitter numbers and `swing.amount` 0.55. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry gives the one-chord and the two-chord bed equal billing — "single-chord or two-chord modal beds (Dorian/Aeolian), so the melody carries all the interest" — and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern"), so a `vamp` weight of 6-of-8 made the two-chord half of that sentence almost unreachable. `vamp` keeps the top weight; the two-chord reading is now reachable at both rates. ⚠ The split between those two rates is **INFERRED** — the entry names the device, not its rate.
